We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1.

We have already applied template 647549 (amide bond formation? Actually it broke amide to give anilide and amine). The apply_template gave precursors: ('COc1cccc(N)c1', 'Nc1c(C(=O)O)nnn1Cc1ccc(CN2CC(F)C2)cc1'). So step 1 retrosynthesis: target -> aniline (methoxy phenyl amine) + heterocycle with carboxylic acid (maybe amide precursor). Actually the product of template is target; precursors are aniline and a heterocycle with carboxylic acid.

Now we need two more steps to get those precursors from simpler building blocks.

First precursor: COc1cccc(N)c1 is anisidine (para? Actually methoxy at position 1, amine at position 4). That's 4-methoxyaniline. Could be obtained via SN2? Actually we can get from 4-bromoanisole via substitution with amine (SN2 aromatic? Actually nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) if electron-withdrawing, but anisole not. Could be via Buchwald-Hartwig amination (not in list). But we have template 1914393 which seems to be a halide substitution: It broke an alkyl halide to give a primary amine? Let's see: template 1914393 retro_smarts: [#7:7]-[C:6]-[c:5]1:[c:4]:[c:3]:[c:2](-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:12]2:[#7;a:11]:[#7;a:10]:[c:14]:[c:13]:2):[c:9]:[c:8]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]1:[c:3]:[c:4]:[c:5](-[C:6]-[#7:7]):[c:8]:[c:9]:1.[#7;a:10]1:[#7;a:11]:[nH;D2;+0:12]:[c:13]:[c:14]:1

So it breaks a C-N bond? Actually forward reaction: Cl-CH2-aryl + heterocycle -> amine attached to heterocycle? Not sure.

But applying to our heterocycle gave precursors: ('FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1', 'Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O'). So second step: heterocycle with carboxylic acid (Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O) and a fluorinated piperidine? Actually FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 is a N-alkylated piperidine with a chlorophenyl.

Now we need to further break those.

Goal: final route 3 reactions total. So we have step1: target -> aniline + heterocycle acid. Step2: heterocycle acid + N-alkyl piperidine -> heterocycle acid? Wait step2 gave two precursors: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 and Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O. So step2 is disconnection of the C-N bond linking heterocycle to the aryl-CH2-piperidine side chain? Actually original target has c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the heterocycle (triazine?) attached via CH2 to phenyl which attached to N4CC(F)C4. So step2 splits that CH2-aryl bond? The template 1914393 seems to break a C-CH2-aryl bond where the CH2 is attached to a heterocycle nitrogen? Not sure.

Now we need to get each of those precursors from simpler ones.

First precursor: COc1cccc(N)c1 (4-methoxyaniline). Could be obtained via substitution of a halide (e.g., 4-bromoanisole) with ammonia (SN2? Actually aromatic SN2 not typical). But we could use a template that breaks a C-N bond to give an aryl halide and amine. Let's search for template that breaks aryl halide to give amine (like aryl halide + amine -> aniline). Use functional_groups_broken ["aryl halide"], functional_groups_formed ["primary amines"] we already looked at 383325 which matches aniline formation from aryl halide? It gave product: COc1cccc(N)c1 from Br-aryl? The template 383325 seems to convert aryl bromide to aniline via nucleophilic substitution with amine? The forward reaction: Br-aryl + O-[N+...]? Actually the reactants include Br-aryl and O-[N+...] (nitro?). Not sure.

But we can use that template in retrosynthesis: target aniline -> aryl bromide + something? Let's check if template 383325 matches COc1cccc(N)c1. We already checked: matches True. So applying template 383325 to COc1cccc(N)c1 will give precursors: likely Br-aryl and something (maybe O-[N+...]?). Let's apply.
